Herb-Roasted Cornish Hens

Served at: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)

Serves 4Prep 15 minCook 1 hr 15 min

Herb-Roasted Cornish Hens are a traditional centerpiece for the Feast of the Holy Innocents, also known as Childermas Banquet, celebrated on December 28th. This dish symbolizes innocence and purity, honoring the children remembered on this solemn day, while offering a comforting and festive meal for family and friends.

Ingredients

  • 2 Cornish hens (about 1 to 1.25 lbs each, 450-570 g)
  • 2 tablespoons olive oil (30 ml)
  • 1 teaspoon salt (5 g)
  • 1/2 teaspoon black pepper (2.5 g)
  • 1 tablespoon fresh rosemary, chopped (15 ml)
  • 1 tablespoon fresh thyme leaves (15 ml)
  • 3 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 lemon, quartered
  • 4 sprigs fresh parsley
  • 1/2 cup chicken broth (120 ml)

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
  2. Rinse the Cornish hens and pat them dry with paper towels.
  3. In a small bowl, combine olive oil, salt, pepper, rosemary, thyme, and minced garlic to create an herb paste.
  4. Rub the herb mixture all over the hens, including inside the cavity.
  5. Stuff each hen’s cavity with lemon quarters and a sprig of parsley.
  6. Place the hens breast side up in a roasting pan and pour chicken broth into the bottom of the pan.
  7. Roast the hens in the preheated oven for about 1 hour and 15 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C) and the skin is golden and crispy.
  8. Baste the hens occasionally with pan juices during roasting to keep them moist.
  9. Remove the hens from the oven and let rest for 10 minutes before serving.

Tips

  • For extra flavor, marinate the hens in the herb mixture for 2-4 hours before roasting.
  • Serve with roasted root vegetables or a winter salad to complement the festive meal.
  • If fresh herbs are unavailable, use 1 teaspoon each of dried rosemary and thyme, but reduce quantity slightly as dried herbs are more concentrated.
